about: Compiler bugs that the human has ruled on, each with a reproducer that was run on the
pinned compiler when it was added (`reference`). The decision log (decision-log.md) holds the reasoning.
A ruling is confirmed when the human has discussed the intended semantics with Modular's
developers; the outcome goes in `confirmation`. If a ruling turns out wrong, the human
`fixed` states what the fixed compiler does, as the human ruled; the model does that.
`upstream.status`: unfiled, filed, fixed-upstream. Only the human files upstream reports.
`nightly` records the last check of the reproducer on a Mojo nightly, before the human meets Modular.

`upstream.tracking` is this project's issue that tracks the report, or the upstream issues that track the bug when others filed it. `upstream.related` lists upstream issues that probably share the bug's cause.
`compiler` says what the current pin, the nightly 1.3.0.dev2026111905 since D-0007, does with the reproducer; `reference` keeps the pin it was ruled at.

bugs.title: xs[i] = f(xs) stores into a stale element when f grows or shrinks xs
bugs.reproducer:
def bump(mut xs: List[Int]) -> Int:
    xs.append(7)
    return 5


def main():
    var xs: List[Int] = [1, 2]
    xs[0] = bump(xs)
    print(xs[0], len(xs))
bugs.compiler: accepts and prints `1 3`, as 1.2.0 did: it locates xs[0] before the call, the append reallocates, and the store of 5 is lost. Built with --sanitize address, AddressSanitizer reports heap-use-after-free

nightly.result: accepts and prints `1 3`; AddressSanitizer reports heap-use-after-free, as on 1.2.0

bugs.title: a struct initialized field by field destroys a field that was never set
bugs.reproducer:
struct Res(Movable):
    var id: Int

    def __init__(out self, id: Int):
        self.id = id

    def __del__(deinit self):
        print("drop", self.id)


struct Two(Movable):
    var a: Res
    var b: Res

    def __init__(out self):
        self.a = Res(1)
        self.b = Res(2)


def main():
    var t: Two
    t.a = Res(1)
    print(t.a.id)
bugs.compiler: prints `1`, `drop 1`, `drop 0`, as 1.2.0 did: it runs the destructor of t.b, which was never initialized
bugs.fixed: rejects the program, as the compiler rejects a variable with a field moved out ("field 't.a' destroyed out of the middle of a value, preventing the overall value from being destroyed"): a variable that ends with only some of its fields set is rejected, however it got there (R, ruled by the human on 2026-11-19)
bugs.model: rejects it as partiallyDestroyed, as the fixed compiler would. The model does not read the deprecated `__del__`, which it rejects as invalidSelf; with `__del__` spelled `__deinit__`, it rejects the program as partiallyDestroyed

confirmation.notes: R, the fixed behaviour ruled on 2026-11-19, is provisional: the human will confirm it with Modular's engineers, and the model changes if that discussion changes the semantics.

bugs.title: @fieldwise_init fails inside a struct cycle through a List, where the hand-written initializer compiles: at the pin with the holder B declared first, on 1.2.0 in either declaration order
bugs.compiler: rejects: "field 'bs' has non-'Deinitable' type 'List[B]'", as 1.2.0 did. With B's initializer written by hand as `def __init__(out self, var a: A): self.a = a^`, it compiles and prints `1`. The forms with A declared first, which 1.2.0 rejected with "invalid implicit move: unexpected keyword argument 'move'" and "invalid call to '__init__': no candidates found", now compile and print `1`
bugs.model: accepts it, as it accepts the hand-written form, and prints `1`

nightly.result: partly fixed: the forms with A declared first compile and print `1`; the reproducer, with B declared first, is still rejected with the same non-'Deinitable' error, and its hand-written form compiles

bugs.title: var x: Int = [e1, ..., en] is accepted for every n, keeps e1 when n >= 2 and crashes at run time when n = 0
bugs.compiler: rejects: "function instantiation failed", with the note "constraint failed: expected 1 elements in the SIMD list literal, found 2" (std/simd.mojo:1094 at 10c54f6f5b), classed noMatchingInit. 1.2.0 accepted it and printed `1`: SIMD's __list_literal__ initializer checked the documented element count only with an assert, which a default build leaves out; `[f(1), f(2)]` evaluated both elements and kept the first, and `var x: Int = []` built and segfaulted (exit 139)
bugs.model: rejects every length but 1, with the class of the position (D-0005); here noMatchingInit

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular

nightly.result: rejected: "function instantiation failed", with the note "constraint failed: expected 1 elements in the SIMD list literal, found 2"; `[f(1), f(2)]` and `[]` (found 0) are rejected the same way. Resolved at the pin (D-0005)

bugs.title: a struct on a cycle through a List is rejected as non-'Deinitable', depending on which structs have a __deinit__ of their own
bugs.compiler: rejects: "field 'children' has non-'Deinitable' type 'List[Node]'", as 1.2.0 did. With `def __deinit__(deinit self): pass` added to Node, it compiles and prints `0`

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular

nightly.result: rejects with the same non-'Deinitable' error, as on 1.2.0, and so do the other suite programs; with the empty __deinit__ it prints `0`

bugs.title: List[Int](range(start, end, step)) aborts when the range is not empty and start - end is ±2^63
bugs.compiler: prints `before`, then aborts: "ABORT: Mojo/stdlib/std/memory/alloc.mojo:1021:18: Layout: `length` must be >= 0". _StridedRange._signed_count computes abs(start - end), which wraps, and List's initializer from an iterable reserves the negative count. 1.2.0 aborts the same way, with "alloc.mojo:888:14: alloc: Layout.count() must be >= 0"
bugs.fixed: builds the range's list, `[-1, 9223372036854775806]`: every element lies between start and end, and only the reserved size overflows

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular

nightly.result: aborts as above; the stdlib's TODO(MSTDL-3087) above _signed_count names the wrap

bugs.title: indexing an Int ignores the index: k[1], k[-1] and k[n] read and write k with no error
bugs.reproducer:
def three() -> Int:
    return 3


def main():
    var k = 7
    print(k[1], k[-1], k[three()])
    k[1] = 5
    print(k)
bugs.compiler: accepts and prints `7 7 7`, then `5`, also with -O0 and -D ASSERT=all: SIMD.__getitem__ and __setitem__ (std/simd.mojo:1193 and 1209 at 10c54f6f5b) lower to pop.simd.extractelement and insertelement with no bounds check, and every index probed acts on the one element
bugs.fixed: checks the index of an Int as the index of an array of length 1, as `var k = [7]` is checked on the pin: a constant index out of range is rejected ("constraint failed: index is out of bounds", or "negative indexing is not supported" when negative), and a computed one fails at run time ("index 3 is out of bounds, valid range is 0 to 0")
bugs.model: rejects the reproducer as constantIndexOutOfBounds, for k[1]; with the constant indices removed, it fails at run time with indexOutOfBounds at k[three()]

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular; its evidence is an analogy with arrays, which neither the docs nor the compiler states for Int

nightly.result: accepts and prints `7 7 7`, then `5`; with `var k = [7]` the constant indices are rejected and k[three()] fails at run time

bugs.title: two one-element arrays compare as equal in an optimized build when a struct's __deinit__ prints
bugs.compiler: prints `del 1`, `del 2`, `True False` in a default build: the arrays compare as equal whatever they hold. With -O0 or -D ASSERT=all it prints the right `False True`. The answers are right when the destructor is `pass`, when the values come from parameters or pop, with two-element arrays, and with plain Ints
bugs.fixed: compares the elements one by one, as the pin does at -O0 and in every control, so it prints `del 1`, `del 2`, `False True`

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular

nightly.result: prints `True False`, as the pin does; Mojo 1.2.0 and the nightly 1.3.0.dev2026111705 do too

bugs.title: a subscript of a struct that declares __getitem__ and __setitem__, on the left of and/or, calls the getter twice when it decides
bugs.compiler: prints `get 0`, `get 0`, `True`, at the default level and -O0: the getter runs to test the operand and again for the result. With a setter the index's values also live until after the getter when the subscript does not decide, and a getter that takes its index `var` is rejected, since its second call uses the temporary the first consumed
bugs.fixed: calls the getter once, with the destroy order of the same struct without __setitem__, so it prints `get 0`, `True`; the human ruled the destroy order and the consumed index part of the bug on 2026-11-21

confirmation.notes: provisional ruling, until the human has discussed it with Modular
